keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Aequi row and the page has no infobox area. The Aequi hold the upper valleys of the Aniene, Tolenus (Turano) and Himella (Salto): the Rieti and L'Aquila provinces and the Roma province without a 40-km disc around Rome (the provinces overshoot to the Marsic and Sabine mountains). Their chief centre, taken about 484 and again about 394, is unnamed on the page; the wars of 484-458 and 394-388 are contests inside this shape, and the shape is lost at once in 304 (Alba Fucens colony 303, Carsioli 302-298). Soft edges.

ledger.note: c. 500 BC: the Aequi 'occupied the upper reaches of the valleys of the Aniene, Tolenus and Himella', east of Latium. No formation date; 500 is a placeholder before the first dated events (their chief centre taken 'about 484 BC', Algidus 458).

ledger.note: c. 394 BC: 'Their chief center is said to have been taken by the Romans about 484 BC and again about 90 years later'; in 389 BC 'the Etruscans, Volsci, and Aequi all raised armies' and Camillus defeated the Aequi; a Roman raid on Aequian territory in 388; then silence 'until 304 BC'. The page does not name the centre (Alba Fucens, an Aequian town, is first a Roman colony in 303).
